findings.title: Active turning away
findings.claim: The ayah presents aversion as an enacted turn away from the signs immediately after reminder, not merely as failure to understand.
findings.mechanism: The completed Form IV verb governs the prepositional object referring back to the signs, turning received contact into a chosen direction of distance.
findings.reader_payoff: Refusal becomes visible as an orientation of the self.
findings.containment: The local sense remains active aversion; honor and worldly-goods pressures are not separate readings.

epistemic.reason: The supplied focus evidence supports the distinct local relation titled "active turning away from signs".

findings.title: Distance from the signs
findings.claim: The prepositional phrase gathers the plural signs into one object from which the person withdraws.
findings.mechanism: The preposition and feminine singular pronoun point back to the plural signs as a collective, giving the turn a defined object and reversing earlier contact.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see exactly what the aversion leaves behind.
findings.containment: This remains a local reference and distance relation; no independent lexical branch is added.

epistemic.reason: The supplied focus evidence supports the distinct local relation titled "separation from the collective signs".

findings.title: Forgetting as a second offense
findings.claim: The conjunction adds forgetting as a second offense after the active turn away.
findings.mechanism: It coordinates the completed aversion with the following completed forgetting, so the second act accumulates on the first instead of restating it.
findings.reader_payoff: The indictment preserves both rejection and loss.
findings.containment: The finding describes local coordination only and does not decide why forgetting occurs.

epistemic.reason: The supplied focus evidence supports the distinct local relation titled "forgetting added to aversion".

findings.title: Culpable forgetting after reminder
findings.claim: The person made to remember becomes the one who loses or abandons the record made by his own agency.
findings.mechanism: The completed forgetting verb governs the open deed clause after reminder and aversion, reversing received reminder at the level of the person's own record.
findings.reader_payoff: Forgetting appears as a culpable break in relation to one's deeds.
findings.containment: Memory loss and abandonment remain co-present possibilities; neither is selected as the sole explanation.

epistemic.reason: The supplied focus evidence supports the distinct local relation titled "forgetting as culpable loss after reminder".

findings.title: Open object of forgetting
findings.claim: The forgotten object remains open enough to cover whatever the person's hands had sent forward.
findings.mechanism: The relative pronoun is the object of forgetting without naming one class of deed, so the following hand-and-action clause supplies breadth.
findings.reader_payoff: The whole output of the person's agency remains in view.
findings.containment: The openness does not assert that every possible action is equally intended or add an external referent.

epistemic.reason: The supplied focus evidence supports the distinct local relation titled "open object of forgotten deeds".

findings.title: Deeds sent ahead
findings.claim: The person's prior acts are pictured as sent ahead into the future that will meet him.
findings.mechanism: The Form II verb makes the deeds go forward as a deposited record, so forgetting affects awareness rather than the deed's prior movement.
findings.reader_payoff: Past agency acquires a forward-facing accountability shape.
findings.containment: The finding stays with the supplied forward-deposit image and adds no unsupplied judgment scene.

epistemic.reason: The supplied focus evidence supports the distinct local relation titled "deeds deposited ahead".

findings.title: The two hands of agency
findings.claim: The dual possessive hands make the forwarded record belong to the person's complete, embodied agency.
findings.mechanism: The dual noun is the agent of the forwarding verb and its possessive suffix binds the record to the person's own instruments of action.
findings.reader_payoff: Accountability becomes something produced with the person's own hands.
findings.containment: The hands idiom supports agency and responsibility here without becoming an exhaustive theory of bodily action.

epistemic.reason: The supplied focus evidence supports the distinct local relation titled "two hands as complete agency".

findings.title: Pivot to divine explanation
findings.claim: The discourse pivots from the offender's sequence to an emphatic divine assertion explaining the blocked response.
findings.mechanism: The emphatic particle and first-person-plural pronoun change the grammatical speaker and introduce the following barriers as asserted causation.
findings.reader_payoff: The ayah moves from indictment into explanation without a new scene.
findings.containment: The finding describes the local discourse pivot and no wider theological system.

epistemic.reason: The supplied focus evidence supports the distinct local relation titled "emphatic divine pivot to explanation".

findings.title: One act, two blockages
findings.claim: The heart coverings and ear heaviness are presented as two faculties under one asserted act of placement.
findings.mechanism: The making verb governs the first object and carries across the coordinated ears clause, linking both barriers under one divine action.
findings.reader_payoff: Cognition and reception appear as paired points in one blocked response system.
findings.containment: The faculties are coordinated, not collapsed into one identical organ or diagnosis.

epistemic.reason: The supplied focus evidence supports the distinct local relation titled "one making verb for two blocked faculties".

findings.title: Coverings upon the hearts
findings.claim: The heart blockage is pictured as coverings resting upon the hearts.
findings.mechanism: The surface preposition places the coverings over the named hearts before the ear clause shifts the geometry inward.

findings.containment: This is a grammatical placement image, not a claim of literal physical veils.

epistemic.reason: The supplied focus evidence supports the distinct local relation titled "coverings upon hearts".

epistemic.reason: The supplied focus evidence supports the distinct local relation titled "purpose-result link to blocked comprehension".
